title: Infinite Night 2 — Built with AI assistance using Codex, Tripo, Blender & Unity. Demo now on Steam!
author: New_Consequence3669
selftext:
Hi everyone! I’m developing **Infinite Night 2** with AI assistance. I use Codex for coding and debugging, and connect **Tripo, Blender, and Unity through MCP** to work on model creation, editing, and integration into the game.

The game features four playable characters, each with their own equipment sets, set bonuses, mastery trees, and weapon upgrades. My main focus is making character progression and experimenting with different builds enjoyable.

Since the previous demo, I’ve improved the combat VFX and character animations. I’m currently refining the controls and interface to make the game more comfortable to play with a controller and on Steam Deck.

**A playable demo is now available on Steam!** If it looks interesting to you, I’d love for you to give it a try and share your thoughts on the combat, character progression, and controls. I’m aiming for a late October release, and your feedback would be a big help. Thanks!

comments.author: Opening_Wafer_6584
comments.body:
Hey, Alex here from the Tripo Studio US team. Really cool seeing Tripo, Blender, and Unity connected through MCP in an actual game that’s already at the Steam demo stage.

I’d be curious how much of the model workflow you’ve managed to automate at this point. When something is generated in Tripo, are you having the MCP pipeline handle most of the Blender editing and Unity integration automatically, or are there still particular steps where you usually jump in manually?

Congrats on getting the demo out too.

replies.author: New_Consequence3669
replies.body:
The entire workflow is 100% AI-automated, from generating 3D models in Tripo to processing them in Blender and integrating them into Unity through MCP. There is no manual human intervention at any stage.
That's why you may still notice some strange or unnatural model animations in the current demo.
